summary: The review switch holds the child-facing contract. With STORYTIME_REVIEW_DRAFT_WEEKS unset, the loader runs the path of round 1: a draft week answers 404, the 404 view names no draft week, and no route shows one. With both review values set to 1, the loader returns w02 to w07 with their imported content, so the taps of P3.8 can run, and the review week w08 stays closed because it holds no books. The switch changed one source file and one test file. No page text, no Thai or English message, and no teacher page changed. Round 1 findings F2 and F3 carry over as nonblocking, and one new Nit records that the P3.8 line for a word with no clip needs a fixture.
nonblocking_findings: F2 [Minor] apps/storytime/app/[locale]/st/[level]/[week]/reader.tsx:368: the tap normalizer is toLowerCase only, and it does not apply the K2 form that apps/storytime/__tests__/look-r3-import.test.ts lines 104 to 110 enforce on the keys. Rationale: a page word with a curly apostrophe or with trailing punctuation would be a visible tap target whose key lookup misses, because the key of the clip holds the straight apostrophe and no outer punctuation. The switch changed no reader line, so the gap of round 1 holds unchanged. A parsed scan of the seven imported week files returns 0 clip keys with an apostrophe and 0 timed words with a character outside a-z, so no child sees a broken tap today. The gap appears when a later week adds such a word.

F3 [Minor] apps/storytime/content/l2/w01.json:1330: the decodable book of w01 holds 11 clip keys, and no app file reads the clip map of the decodable book. Rationale: the decodable word tap still cuts the sentence recording at apps/storytime/app/[locale]/st/[level]/[week]/decodable.tsx line 501, so the vowel-link defect of the 'a nurse' pair stays on the decodable page. The phase introduced the data, and the decodable behaviour is pre-existing from Phase 1 and Phase 2. The switch changed no decodable line. The decodable page sits outside the Phase 3 acceptance, so no phase gate fails.

F4 [Nit] measure/tracks/storytime_look_20261107/test-strategy.md:830: the browser review taps one word per week of w02 to w07 that holds a clip and one word that holds no clip, and it records tap_<week>=own_clip|no_clip_target for each of the seven lines. Rationale: a parsed scan of the seven imported week files returns 0 timed words without a clip in every book, so the shipped data holds no word with no clip. The P3.8 line of a word with no clip therefore needs a fixture, or the report records that the property holds for every word of the week. The browser review role owns the fixture and the line, so the fact is no blocker of this review.

With STORYTIME_REVIEW_DRAFT_WEEKS=1 and STORYTIME_SHOW_DRAFT_MEDIA=1, apps/storytime/lib/content.ts line 130 judges the draft week by the published rules, line 134 finds no missing picture, line 141 names the audio and song parts, line 142 opens the draft media, and line 144 writes the log line storytime week <key> shows a draft week (review switch). The loader then returns each of w02 to w07 with its imported content, and line 169 applies the same rule in highestOpenWeeks().

apps/storytime/content/l2/w08.json holds an empty books array and the status draft. The published rules of apps/storytime/lib/readiness.ts keep a week with no books out of the app, so the review switch does not open w08 and the local review stays on the six imported weeks.

The week files name the clip paths as l2/media/wNN/words/, and the media root of each week holds the same tree, for example l2/media/w02/words/wa-how.mp3 under the root of the w02 package. The clip of each tap word therefore resolves through the local media root when the storage stand-in serves that root, with STORYTIME_MEDIA_BASE=gs://storytime-app-media and STORYTIME_STORAGE_ENDPOINT set to the stand-in.

The browser review pattern comes from apps/storytime/__tests__/look-phase2-browser-gate.sh lines 2020 to 2094: a stand-in for the storage serves one media root on a free port, and the app starts with next build and next start from apps/storytime/package.json. The local review copy sets STORYTIME_REVIEW_DRAFT_WEEKS=1, STORYTIME_SHOW_DRAFT_MEDIA=1, STORYTIME_CONTENT_DIR at the content folder of the copy, and the four storage values.
The tap word of each week of round 1 holds still, because no content file changed: w02 How, w03 It, w04 This, w05 I, w06 cat, w07 ball, and w01 Hello.
A parsed scan of the seven imported week files returns 0 timed words without a clip in every book, so the P3.8 line of each week reads own_clip. The no_clip_target line needs a fixture.

apps/storytime/app/[locale]/st/[level]/[week]/reader.tsx line 368 builds the tap key with toLowerCase, and line 530 builds the visible target with the same normalizer, so the visible target and the played clip always agree.
